q: On the orders of the Engineer, a portion of work already executed and covered up is opened up for inspection and testing, and the work is found to be defective and not in accordance with the contract. In such a case, the cost of the opening up, testing and making good is borne by:

options.A: The contractor
options.B: The Railways, in every case, because the opening up was ordered by the Engineer
options.C: The contractor and the Railways in equal shares
options.D: The insurance company with which the work is insured

q: A 'pile cap' in the foundation of a structure is:

options.A: The protective cap provided on the top of a single pile to receive the hammer blows during driving
options.B: The cutting edge provided at the bottom of a pile
options.C: The layer of lean concrete laid under an isolated footing
options.D: The concrete slab cast over the heads of a group of piles, which distributes the load of the column or pier over all the piles of the group

q: The cost of the stamp paper and of the execution of the formal agreement of a works contract is ordinarily borne by:

options.A: The Railways, as a charge to the work
options.B: The contractor
options.C: The Railways and the contractor in equal shares
options.D: The Tender Committee which recommended the award

q: 'Dewatering' carried out in connection with the foundation work of a bridge or a building refers to:

options.A: Pumping out or otherwise removing water from the foundation excavation or enclosure, so that the foundation work can be carried out in the dry
options.B: Providing permanent drains around the completed foundation
options.C: Lowering the highest flood level of the stream by training works
options.D: Supplying water to the site for curing of the concrete work

q: The daily diary maintained by the engineering official in direct charge of a work at the site primarily records:

options.A: The personal movements and leave of the staff posted at the site
options.B: The correspondence exchanged between the division and the headquarters on the work
options.C: The day-to-day progress of the work, the labour and materials deployed, the hindrances encountered and the inspections made
options.D: The bills passed and payments made to the contractor from day to day

q: A 'dumpy level', used in the survey and execution of railway works, is an instrument which is used for:

options.A: Measuring horizontal and vertical angles at a point
options.B: Determining the levels of points, that is, their heights with reference to a datum
options.C: Measuring the distance between two points along the alignment
options.D: Determining the direction of the magnetic meridian at a point

q: Consider the following statements: 1. Where a party to a contract renounces it before the time fixed for its performance, the other party may treat the contract as at an end and claim damages at once, without waiting for the due date of performance. 2. In such a case, the other party is bound in every case to wait until the due date of performance before it can claim any damages. Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A 'box culvert' provided under a railway embankment is:

options.A: A culvert formed of large-diameter pipes laid side by side
options.B: An open channel lined with stone pitching
options.C: A drainage structure of box section in reinforced cement concrete, cast in situ or pre-cast, through which the drainage passes under the embankment
options.D: A submersible causeway over which flood water flows

q: Works of residential quarters, though excepted from the normal test of financial remunerativeness, are expected to satisfy the condition relating to assessed rent. The assessed rent of such quarters is worked out with reference to:

options.A: The market rent of similar private houses in the locality
options.B: A prescribed percentage return on the capital cost of the quarters
options.C: The licence fee paid by the occupants of similar quarters in the past
options.D: The plinth area of the quarters alone, irrespective of their cost

q: A 'well foundation', commonly adopted for major railway bridges, is a foundation in which:

options.A: A hollow well of masonry or concrete is sunk into the ground at the site, filled and capped, so that the load of the pier is carried to a deep firm stratum
options.B: A large pit is excavated and filled with boulders in layers
options.C: A raft of concrete is spread over the whole area under the pier at a shallow depth
options.D: Timber piles are driven in a group and connected by a grillage of steel beams

q: The 'steining' of a well foundation of a bridge is:

options.A: The steel cutting edge provided at the bottom of the well to help it sink
options.B: The wall of masonry or concrete forming the hollow shell of the well, which is built up in height as the well sinks into the ground
options.C: The filling of sand or concrete placed inside the well after it has been sunk to the required depth
options.D: The concrete cap cast over the top of the well to receive the pier

q: The 'bed block' provided at the top of a bridge pier or abutment is:

options.A: The block of stone or concrete on which the bearing of the girder rests, distributing the load from the bearing over the masonry below
options.B: The deepest block of the foundation laid below the scour level
options.C: The block provided at the end of the approach slab of the bridge
options.D: The block anchoring the guard rails on the bridge deck

q: Under the conditions of a works contract, compliance with the bye-laws and requirements of the local authorities applicable to the work, and payment of the fees and charges levied thereunder, is the responsibility of:

options.A: The Railways, in every case
options.B: The Engineer personally
options.C: The contractor, at his own cost
options.D: The local authority itself, which waives such charges for railway works

q: The 'head wall' provided at the end of a culvert is a wall which:

options.A: Retains the embankment at the inlet or outlet end of the culvert and guides the drainage into or out of the culvert barrel
options.B: Carries the track over the middle of the culvert barrel
options.C: Divides a wide culvert into two separate barrels
options.D: Protects the top of the embankment from rain cuts

q: The muster roll and the register of wages which a works contractor is required to maintain in respect of the labour engaged by him serve to:

options.A: Fix the rates payable for the items of the work
options.B: Record the measurements of the work executed by each labourer
options.C: Replace the attendance register of the departmental staff at the site
options.D: Evidence the labour actually employed and the wages paid to them, for inspection by the Engineer and the labour authorities

q: In a turnout, the 'toe' of the switch is:

options.A: The thick end of the switch rail, which is fixed at the heel
options.B: The distance between the two switch rails at the heel
options.C: The thin, movable front end of the switch rail, from which the switch begins at the stock rail
options.D: The end of the crossing farthest from the switch

q: The Works Abstract compiled in the Accounts office in connection with works expenditure is:

options.A: A monthly abstract summarising the expenditure booked on works under the several heads of allocation, for incorporation in the general books of account
options.B: An abstract of the measurements recorded in the Measurement Books of all works
options.C: A summary of the tenders received for works during the month
options.D: An abstract of the estimates sanctioned during the month

q: In chain surveying for a proposed railway work, an 'offset' is:

options.A: The distance measured along the chain line from the starting point
options.B: The angle between the chain line and the magnetic meridian
options.C: The lateral distance of a point or feature from the chain line, measured ordinarily at right angles to it, for locating the feature on the plan
options.D: The difference in level between two points on the chain line

q: In the estimate prepared for the dismantling or demolition of an existing asset, provision is made for credit on account of the materials expected to be released from the asset. The effect of this credit is that:

options.A: The gross cost of the dismantling work is increased by the value of the released materials
options.B: The sanction of the competent authority is sought for the net cost of the dismantling, after taking the credit for the released materials into account
options.C: The released materials become the property of the agency executing the dismantling
options.D: The dismantling work can be executed without any sanctioned estimate

q: The 'centre line method' used in preparing the detailed estimate of a building work is a method of computing quantities in which:

options.A: The quantities are worked out from the centre line of the site boundary
options.B: Only the walls on the centre line of the building are measured
options.C: The measurements are taken along the centre line of the thickness of the walls only at the plinth level
options.D: The total centre line length of the walls is computed once and is multiplied by the breadth and the height or depth of each item, with adjustments at junctions, to arrive at its quantity

q: In connection with track renewal works, the abbreviation TTR stands for:

options.A: Through Turnout Renewal
options.B: Through Tie Renewal
options.C: Total Track Renewal
options.D: Temporary Track Repair

q: A 'levelling course' provided under the foundation or footing of a structure consists of:

options.A: A course of brickwork laid at the plinth level of the structure
options.B: A layer of stone ballast spread under the track formation
options.C: A layer of lean or plain concrete laid at the bottom of the foundation to provide a level and firm base for the footing and to keep it clear of the soil
options.D: A course of masonry provided at the top of the foundation for receiving the superstructure

q: Before a completion report of a work is sanctioned by the competent authority, the figures of cost and the allocation shown in it are subjected to:

options.A: Verification by the contractor who executed the work
options.B: Check by the Accounts office, for the correctness of the cost booked and of the allocation adopted
options.C: Approval of the Tender Committee which awarded the work
options.D: Countersignature by the Commissioner of Railway Safety

q: A 'partition wall' provided inside a building is a wall which:

options.A: Divides the internal space of the building into rooms or areas and carries no load except its own weight
options.B: Carries the load of the roof and the floors above it to the foundation
options.C: Retains the earth on one side of it in a cutting
options.D: Forms the outer enclosure of the building against the weather

q: A contractor has applied for extension of the period of completion of a work, and his application is still under consideration. In this position, the contractor:

options.A: May suspend the work until the extension is decided
options.B: May slow down the work in proportion to the extension applied for
options.C: Is entitled to treat the contract as closed on the original date of completion
options.D: Must continue to execute the work in accordance with the contract, the pendency of his application not entitling him to suspend or slow down the work

q: The 'chords' of a steel truss used in a bridge or a roof are:

options.A: The diagonal members connecting the top and bottom members of the truss
options.B: The vertical members provided at the ends of the truss
options.C: The principal top and bottom members of the truss, between which the web members are arranged
options.D: The cross girders carrying the deck of the bridge

q: In an EPC contract for a major project, the 'appointed date' from which the period for completion of the project is reckoned is the date:

options.A: On which the Letter of Acceptance is issued to the contractor
options.B: Declared by the Authority after the conditions precedent, such as availability of the land and right of way for the work, have been fulfilled
options.C: On which the contractor submits his detailed design for the project
options.D: On which the first stage payment is made to the contractor

q: 'Bracing' provided in a steel girder bridge or a steel structure serves mainly to:

options.A: Resist lateral forces such as wind and to keep the structure stable against lateral movement
options.B: Carry the vertical load of the trains from the girders to the piers
options.C: Provide a footpath for the inspection staff along the bridge
options.D: Connect the rails to the sleepers on the bridge deck

q: In an EPC contract, the scope of the work is defined by the requirements and performance specifications given by the Authority. Where the Authority requires a change which lies outside that defined scope, the change is dealt with:

options.A: As an ordinary variation at the rates of the schedule of rates, the EPC contract having no separate procedure for it
options.B: By the contractor at his own cost, as all design responsibility rests with him
options.C: By rejecting the change, an EPC contract admitting of no change after its award
options.D: Under the change of scope procedure of the contract, with adjustment of the contract price and, where justified, of the completion period

q: The 'grip length' provided in a well or pile foundation of a bridge is:

options.A: The length of the foundation which remains above the highest flood level
options.B: The length of the pier between the foundation and the bearing
options.C: The depth of the foundation provided below the maximum scour level, so that the foundation remains safely held in the ground even after scour
options.D: The length of the approach slab behind the abutment

q: A board displayed at the site of a public work in progress ordinarily shows, for public information:

options.A: The names of the members of the Tender Committee which awarded the work
options.B: The rates quoted by all the tenderers for the work
options.C: The internal file references under which the estimate of the work was sanctioned
options.D: The name of the work, the name of the executing agency or contractor, the cost of the work and its stipulated period of completion

q: A 'sunken slab' provided in the toilets and bathrooms of a building is a slab which is:

options.A: Cast at a level lower than the adjoining floor level, so that the drainage pipes and the waterproofing and flooring of the wet area can be accommodated within the depth so available
options.B: Cast without any reinforcement, as it carries no load
options.C: Provided only in the foundations of the building
options.D: Sloped towards the centre of the room for cleaning purposes

q: The Engineer orders the suspension of a work for a period for reasons which are not attributable to the contractor. On the resumption of the work, the contractor is entitled, under the contract, to:

options.A: Payment of the full value of the unexecuted work as compensation
options.B: Revision of all his rates to the current schedule rates
options.C: A corresponding extension of the period of completion, covering the period of the suspension so ordered
options.D: Determination of the contract at his option in every case

q: A 'string course' provided in a building is:

options.A: A course of masonry laid below the foundation to spread the load
options.B: A vertical groove cut in a wall for concealing pipes and cables
options.C: The course of bricks laid on edge to form the top of a foundation
options.D: A horizontal band of masonry or concrete, projecting slightly from the face of the wall, provided at a floor level or as a stringing course on the facade

q: A tenderer submits his tender for a work without furnishing the earnest money required under the tender conditions, and he does not belong to any category exempted from furnishing it. Such a tender is liable to be:

options.A: Accepted, the earnest money being recovered from his first running bill
options.B: Accepted after obtaining the earnest money from him after the opening of the tenders
options.C: Considered after obtaining the approval of the Tender Committee for the omission
options.D: Rejected summarily, as a tender not accompanied by the required earnest money is not a valid tender

q: At the close of a financial year, work on a sanctioned work has been executed and measured, but the contractor's bill for it has not been passed or paid before 31st March. To bring the liability into the accounts of the year in which the work was done, the amount is:

options.A: Ignored altogether, as no payment was made during the year
options.B: Held permanently under a suspense head without being charged to the work
options.C: Charged to the grant of the next financial year as a fresh work
options.D: Provided for as a demand payable at the close of the year, so that the expenditure is accounted for in that year itself

q: A work is executed by the Railways as a deposit work for an outside party which has deposited the estimated cost in advance. The expenditure on such a work is incurred:

options.A: Against the voted grant of the Railways, the deposit being treated as a loan to the Railways
options.B: By the party itself, the Railways only supervising the work
options.C: Against the amount deposited by the party and held in the deposit head, and not as a charge on the Railways' own grant for its works
options.D: Against the Depreciation Reserve Fund, to be recovered from the party later

q: In the classification of works expenditure, the Plan Head of a work and the fund from which it is financed serve different purposes, in that:

options.A: The Plan Head indicates the source from which money is borrowed for the work
options.B: The fund indicates the detailed head under which the asset is recorded in the Block Account
options.C: Both the Plan Head and the fund are interchangeable descriptions of the same thing
options.D: The Plan Head classifies the work according to its nature or purpose, while the fund, such as Capital, Depreciation Reserve Fund or Development Fund, indicates the source from which the expenditure is met

q: Measurement Books used for recording the measurements of works are issued to the officials concerned against:

options.A: A numerical account of the books issued, so that every book issued can be traced, accounted for and got back after use
options.B: A simple verbal requisition, no record of issue being necessary
options.C: Entries made in the Contractor's Ledger of the division
options.D: The personal security deposit furnished by the official

q: After payment has been made to a contractor for the measurements recorded in a Measurement Book, those measurements are dealt with in the book so as to prevent their being used again for another payment. This is done by:

options.A: Scoring off or cancelling the measurements so paid for, with a reference to the bill in which payment was made
options.B: Tearing out the pages containing the measurements so paid for
options.C: Rewriting the measurements in a fresh Measurement Book
options.D: Obtaining the contractor's signature again on a blank page

q: At the final closure of a works contract, after the final bill has been passed and all advances and recoveries have been adjusted, the balance shown against the contractor in the Contractor's Ledger should be:

options.A: A large debit balance representing the profit of the contract
options.B: A credit balance representing the earnest money of all tenderers
options.C: Nil, there being nothing further recoverable from or payable to the contractor under that contract
options.D: Transferred permanently to the Works Register of another work

q: A contractor's on-account bill put up to the Accounts office for internal check is required to be accompanied, besides the bill itself, by:

options.A: The measurements recorded in the Measurement Book, the abstract of measurements prepared from them and the statement of recoveries due from the contractor
options.B: The original tender notice published in the newspapers
options.C: The personal file of the Engineer-in-charge of the work
options.D: The balance sheet of the contractor's firm for the previous year

q: Departmental materials are issued from a stores depot to a works contractor for incorporation in a work, their cost being recoverable from him. Until the cost is recovered from his bills, the amount is held in the works accounts:

options.A: As a final charge to the work, no recovery being necessary thereafter
options.B: Under Miscellaneous Works Advances, as an amount outstanding for recovery from the contractor
options.C: As earnings of the Railways for the year
options.D: Under the earnest money deposit account of the contractor

q: The original grant allotted for a work is Rs 600 lakh. During the year, a supplementary grant of Rs 45 lakh is obtained for the work, and Rs 30 lakh is surrendered from the work. The final grant for the work is:

options.A: Rs 585 lakh
options.B: Rs 645 lakh
options.C: Rs 675 lakh
options.D: Rs 615 lakh

q: The total value of supply under a works contract is Rs 8,00,000, which exceeds the prescribed threshold of Rs 2.5 lakh. The tax deducted at source under the GST law, at the rate of 2 per cent, on payment made to the contractor amounts to:
Before the final bill of a works contract is paid, the amount of the bill is agreed with the Contractor's Ledger mainly in order to ensure that:

options.A: The contractor has executed other works also for the same division
options.B: No advance made to the contractor remains unrecovered and no recovery due from him is left unadjusted at the final settlement
options.C: The contractor's earnest money can be forfeited at that stage
options.D: The measurements can be recorded afresh in a new Measurement Book

q: In preparing the detailed estimate of a building by the long wall and short wall method, the quantities of items such as earthwork and masonry are computed by:

options.A: Taking the plinth area of the building and multiplying it by a single rate
options.B: Measuring only the external faces of the walls of the building
options.C: Treating the long walls and the short walls of the building separately, the lengths of the long walls and short walls being worked out from the centre line dimensions with the prescribed adjustments for junctions
options.D: Adopting the quantities of a similar building executed earlier, without any measurement

q: A sanction order issued by a competent authority for expenditure on a work is required to indicate, among other things:

options.A: The names of the contractors likely to tender for the work
options.B: The date on which the next budget of the Railways will be presented
options.C: The head of account or allocation to which the expenditure is debitable
options.D: The market rates of all materials to be used on the work

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where the Schedule of Powers prescribes the concurrence of Finance for the exercise of a power, a sanction issued without obtaining that concurrence is incomplete and not fully effective.
2. The concurrence of Finance, where prescribed, is a mere formality which can be dispensed with by the sanctioning authority at its discretion.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A renewal work also involves an element of improvement of the asset to a higher standard, so that its cost is chargeable partly to Capital and partly to Revenue or the Depreciation Reserve Fund. In such a case, the estimate of the work is required to:

options.A: Show the whole cost under Capital alone, the apportionment being made after completion
options.B: Show separately the portion of the cost chargeable to each head of allocation, so that the expenditure can be booked correctly as it is incurred
options.C: Be sanctioned twice, once as a capital work and again as a revenue work
options.D: Omit the improvement element altogether from the estimate

q: Where land has to be acquired for a railway project, the cost of acquiring that land is treated in the project accounts as:

options.A: A part of the estimated cost of the project itself, provided for in its estimate and charged to the project
options.B: A charge on the general revenues of the State Government in every case
options.C: A deposit work executed for the revenue department of the State
options.D: An item to be met from the contingencies of other sanctioned works

q: The detailed estimate of a work, besides its report, specifications and detailed measurements, is accompanied by:

options.A: The tenders received for similar works in the past
options.B: A certificate from the contractor proposed to be engaged
options.C: The names of the officials who will supervise the work
options.D: The drawings and plans of the proposed work, from which the quantities in the estimate are worked out

q: The allotment of funds made for a work in the budget of a particular year is ordinarily fixed with reference to:

options.A: The total sanctioned cost of the work, the whole of which is allotted in the first year itself
options.B: The balance of the earnest money held from contractors of the division
options.C: The expenditure expected to be incurred on the work during that year, having regard to its programme and progress
options.D: The amount of the security deposits expected to be refunded during the year

q: In working out the financial justification of a project, the test of remunerativeness, namely the minimum rate of return required, is applied with reference to:

options.A: The anticipated return on the initial estimated cost of the project
options.B: The return on the book value of the assets of the whole Railway
options.C: The interest paid by the Railways on their market borrowings alone
options.D: The savings expected in the establishment charges of the division

q: The sanctioned estimate of a work is Rs 5.00 crore. On completion, the cost of the work is anticipated to be Rs 5.60 crore. The excess over the sanctioned estimate, expressed as a percentage of the sanctioned estimate, is:

options.A: 10 per cent
options.B: 15 per cent
options.C: 12 per cent
options.D: 20 per cent

q: A railway project involves a capital investment of Rs 200 crore. Its anticipated gross earnings are Rs 45 crore per annum and the anticipated working expenses are Rs 25 crore per annum. The anticipated rate of return on the capital invested is:

options.A: 10 per cent
options.B: 22.5 per cent
options.C: 12.5 per cent
options.D: 8 per cent

q: A deposit work is executed by the Railways at a cost of Rs 60,00,000. Departmental charges are leviable on the work at 12.5 per cent of the cost. The total amount recoverable from the party on whose behalf the work is executed is:
Earthwork in an embankment is executed over a length of 250 metres, with an average cross-sectional area of 10 square metres. The quantity of earthwork executed is:

options.A: 250 cubic metres
options.B: 2,500 cubic metres
options.C: 2,000 cubic metres
options.D: 25,000 cubic metres

q: A tenderer, while filling in his tender for a work, makes a correction or overwriting in the rates quoted by him. For such a correction to be taken into account, it must be:

options.A: Made only in pencil so that it can be altered later
options.B: Certified by the Engineer-in-charge of the work
options.C: Attested by the initials of the tenderer himself
options.D: Noted by the tender committee after the tenders are opened

q: In the evaluation of the tenders received for a work, the bids are first examined for responsiveness to the tender conditions, and the position is that:

options.A: The prices of all bids received, responsive or not, are compared together to find the lowest offer
options.B: A bid which is not substantially responsive to the tender conditions is set aside, and the prices of the responsive bids alone are compared for deciding the lowest acceptable offer
options.C: Responsiveness is examined only after the work has been awarded
options.D: A non-responsive bid can be made responsive by holding negotiations with the tenderer

q: For certain items of a work, a tenderer has quoted rates which are abnormally low and unbalanced in relation to the estimated rates, so that the quantities actually executed may cause loss to the Railways. In such a case, the accepting authority may safeguard the Railways by:

options.A: Rejecting the tenderer's earnest money and returning his security deposit
options.B: Paying him at the estimated rates instead of his quoted rates
options.C: Requiring him to furnish an additional security for the due performance of the contract in respect of such items
options.D: Reducing the quantities of the work after the contract is awarded

q: Start-ups recognised by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade are, in Government procurement, exempted from furnishing:

options.A: The performance guarantee for a work awarded to them
options.B: The earnest money deposit for participating in a tender
options.C: Any bill for the work executed by them
options.D: The income tax deductible on their bills

q: A tenderer claims exemption from furnishing the earnest money deposit on the ground that he belongs to an exempted category. To avail of the exemption, he is required to:

options.A: Merely declare the exemption orally before the tender committee
options.B: Obtain a separate exemption order from the Railway Board for that tender
options.C: Pay the earnest money first and claim its refund after the award of the work
options.D: Produce, along with his tender, the proof or certificate showing that he belongs to the exempted category

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where all the tenders received for a work are rejected by the competent authority, the reasons for such rejection should be recorded.
2. The competent authority may reject all the tenders received for a work without recording any reason, as acceptance of any tender is not obligatory on the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A tenderer submits tenders for several works of a division which are tendered at about the same time. While deciding whether a further work can be awarded to him, his bid capacity is assessed:

options.A: Cumulatively, taking into account the value of the works already in his hand and their remaining period of execution, so that he is not awarded work beyond his capacity
options.B: Work by work, ignoring the works already in his hand
options.C: Only with reference to the earnest money furnished by him
options.D: Only with reference to the number of his employees on the rolls

q: Where the Notice Inviting Tender for a work so permits, a tenderer may quote for a part of the work or for some only of the works included in the tender. Where the tender does not so permit:

options.A: The tenderer may still quote for any part he chooses, and the Railways must accept it
options.B: A tender which does not cover the whole of the work as invited is liable to be treated as not responsive to the tender
options.C: The tender committee must split the work to suit the tenderer
options.D: The earnest money of such a tenderer is refunded with interest

q: The Letter of Acceptance issued to the successful tenderer for a work ordinarily specifies, among other things:

options.A: The names of all the unsuccessful tenderers for the work
options.B: The date on which the next tender for a similar work will be invited
options.C: The value of the contract and the period within which the work is to be completed
options.D: The profit which the contractor is expected to earn on the work

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The earnest money of the unsuccessful tenderers is refunded to them after the tender has been decided.
2. Interest is payable by the Railways to the tenderers on the earnest money for the period it remained with the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A number of connected works are grouped and tendered together in packages, and the tender conditions permit tenderers to quote for one or more packages. In such a case:

options.A: Every tenderer is bound to quote for all the packages together
options.B: A tenderer may quote for any one or more of the packages, and the packages may be awarded to different tenderers on the basis of the evaluation made as per the tender conditions
options.C: All the packages must necessarily be awarded to a single tenderer
options.D: The earnest money is payable only by the tenderer who gets all the packages

q: A dispute has arisen between a works contractor and the Railways and has been taken up for settlement under the contract. Pending the settlement of the dispute, the contractor:

options.A: May stop the work at once on his own authority
options.B: Is entitled to withhold the materials supplied by the Railways
options.C: Cannot be required to do any further work under the contract
options.D: Is required to continue the execution of the work in accordance with the contract, the dispute being pursued separately

q: Notices and orders which the Railways are required to serve on a contractor under a works contract are ordinarily served:

options.A: Only through a court of law
options.B: Through the contractor's bankers in every case
options.C: By affixing them at the site office of the Engineer alone
options.D: At the address of the contractor given in the contract, a notice so sent to that address being treated as duly served on him

q: Before a contractor brings to the site materials such as stone, ballast or bricks which he proposes to use on a work, the source from which the materials are to be obtained is required to be:

options.A: Kept secret by the contractor until the final bill is paid
options.B: Decided by the tender committee after the work is awarded
options.C: Approved by the Engineer, so that the quality of the materials from that source is ascertained before they are used on the work
options.D: Notified to the Railway Board in every case

q: The arrangements for reaching the site of a work, such as the making of a temporary approach for the movement of his men and materials, are ordinarily:

options.A: Made by the contractor at his own cost, unless the contract expressly provides for their being made by the Railways
options.B: Made by the Railways free of cost for every contractor
options.C: Charged to the contingencies of the sanctioned estimate in all cases
options.D: Arranged by the tender committee before the tenders are opened

q: Before a works contractor commences the work, the insurance policies which he is required to take out under the contract are ordinarily:

options.A: Kept by the contractor in his own office, and need never be shown to the Railways
options.B: Produced before the Engineer for inspection and record, and kept in force during the currency of the contract
options.C: Furnished only after the final bill of the work has been paid
options.D: Taken out in the name of the contractor's bankers

q: A works contract has been determined on account of the contractor's default. In regard to the site of the work, the contractor is required to:

options.A: Retain possession of the site until all his claims are settled
options.B: Hand over the site to the Railways and remove his materials, tools and plant from it within the period allowed to him, failing which the Railways may remove them at his cost
options.C: Sell the site materials to another contractor of his choice
options.D: Continue the balance work departmentally on behalf of the Railways

q: The setting out of a work by the contractor is checked by the Engineer or his representative as the work proceeds. The effect of such a check is that:

options.A: The responsibility for any error in the setting out passes wholly to the Railways
options.B: The contractor is absolved of all responsibility for the accuracy of the work
options.C: The contractor remains responsible for the correct setting out of the work, the check by the Engineer not relieving him of that responsibility
options.D: The measurements of the work need not be recorded thereafter

q: Extra items of work executed by a contractor on the written orders of the Engineer are recorded in the Measurement Book:

options.A: Together with the original items, without any separate identification
options.B: Only after the final bill of the work has been passed
options.C: In the personal diary of the contractor alone
options.D: Separately, with a reference to the order under which the item was executed, so that the payment for it can be checked against that order

q: The value of durable materials brought to the site of a work by a contractor is Rs 10,00,000. The maximum secured advance payable to him against these materials, at 75 per cent of their value, is:

The value of a works contract is Rs 50,00,000. Completion of the work is delayed by 5 weeks for reasons attributable to the contractor. The liquidated damages leviable at 0.5 per cent of the contract value per week amount to:

In a works contract, the amount of work done against the labour component is Rs 15,00,000. The cost index for labour rises from 200 at the time of tendering to 220 for the period of the bill. The price variation payable on the labour component is:
In a contractor's bill for a work, the total recoveries and deductions due from him exceed the gross value of the work done covered by the bill. Such a bill is worked out as:

options.A: A bill payable to the contractor for the gross value, the recoveries being ignored
options.B: A minus (negative) bill, the net amount being recoverable from the contractor or adjusted against his other dues or security
options.C: A secured advance bill for the amount of the recoveries
options.D: A first and final bill closing the contract

q: A 'king closer' used in brickwork is:

options.A: A brick with one corner cut away diagonally, used next to the queen closer at the corner of a wall to maintain the bond
options.B: A full brick laid across the thickness of the wall at a corner
options.C: A brick cut to half its length for use at a stopped end
options.D: A defective brick rejected for use in the face of a wall

q: A detailed estimate of a work is accompanied by a lead statement. This statement primarily shows:

options.A: The names of the officers who will supervise the execution of the work
options.B: The rates quoted by tenderers for similar works executed earlier
options.C: The sources from which the principal materials for the work are to be obtained and the leads, that is the distances of carriage involved, forming the basis of the provision for carriage in the estimate
options.D: The allotment of funds available for the work during the year

q: In levelling work for a proposed railway work, a 'foresight' is:

options.A: The first staff reading taken after the level instrument is set up, on a point of known reduced level
options.B: A staff reading taken on an intermediate point for preparing a cross-section
options.C: The difference between the back sight and the intermediate sight at a station
options.D: The staff reading taken on a point whose reduced level is to be determined, ordinarily the last reading taken from that setting of the instrument

q: At the opening of the tenders received for a work, the rates and amounts quoted by the tenderers are dealt with by the tender-opening officials in the manner that:

options.A: The rates and amounts are encircled in the tender documents and the officials sign or initial the documents and every correction appearing in them, so that no alteration can be made afterwards
options.B: The rates are rewritten by the officials in a separate register and the tender documents are returned to the tenderers
options.C: The tender documents are kept unsigned, corrections being attested only after the tender is accepted
options.D: The rates are announced to all the tenderers present, who may then revise their offers

q: A 'strap footing' provided in the foundation of a building is a footing in which:

options.A: A single footing is spread under the whole area of the building
options.B: Two isolated footings are connected by a beam, called the strap, which helps in distributing the loads of the two columns over their footings
options.C: A continuous footing runs along the whole length of a load-bearing wall
options.D: A group of piles is capped by a common concrete slab

q: Tax has been deducted at source from the bills paid to a works contractor. In respect of the tax so deducted, the contractor is entitled to:

options.A: A refund of the tax from the division in cash at the close of the work
options.B: An enhancement of his contract rates by the amount of the tax
options.C: Receive a certificate of the tax deducted at source from the Railways, so that he can claim credit for it in his income-tax assessment
options.D: Furnish a fresh performance guarantee for the amount of the tax

q: A 'construction joint' provided in concrete work is a joint which is:

options.A: Provided across the whole structure to allow its expansion and contraction with temperature
options.B: Formed at the junction of a wall with the floor slab of a building
options.C: Cut in the surface of a concrete pavement to control cracking due to shrinkage
options.D: Formed where concreting is stopped at the end of a stage of work and is resumed later, the joint being located and treated so that the strength of the structure is not weakened

q: The application made for the sanction of the Commissioner of Railway Safety for opening a newly constructed line for the public carriage of passengers is accompanied, among other documents, by:

options.A: The comparative statement of the tenders received for the construction of the line
options.B: A safety certificate signed by the responsible officers, certifying that the line can be opened for passenger traffic without danger to the public
options.C: The completion report of every work comprised in the project
options.D: The final bill of the contractor who constructed the line

q: The balances appearing against the individual contractors in the Contractor's Ledger are agreed with the corresponding head in the general books of account through:

options.A: A broadsheet prepared periodically, in which the ledger balances are summarised and reconciled with the general books, differences being investigated and set right
options.B: The deviation statement prepared at the final bill stage of each contract
options.C: The comparative statement of the tenders received during the month
options.D: The Material-at-Site statements of the works under execution in the division

q: A 'plinth beam' provided in a framed building is a beam which is:

options.A: Provided at the top of the parapet to carry the load of the roof
options.B: Laid below the foundation to spread the load of the wall on the soil
options.C: Provided at the plinth level connecting the columns or footings, which supports the wall over it and ties the footings together against unequal settlement
options.D: Provided over a door opening to carry the masonry above the opening

q: Under the bay method of preparing an approximate estimate of a building, the rough cost of the building is arrived at by:

options.A: Multiplying the plinth area of the building by the rate per unit of plinth area
options.B: Multiplying the cubic content of the building by the rate per unit volume
options.C: Taking a fixed amount for every person who will occupy the building
options.D: Working out the cost of one typical bay of a repetitive framed structure and multiplying it by the number of bays in the building

q: In levelling work, a 'change point' (turning point) is a point:

options.A: On which both a foresight from the previous setting of the instrument and a back sight from the next setting are taken, when the instrument is shifted during levelling
options.B: At which the alignment of the proposed line changes its direction
options.C: Whose reduced level is adopted as the datum for the whole survey
options.D: From which the cross-section of the formation is taken at right angles to the alignment

q: A works tender specifies the facilities and items which the Railways will provide for the work, such as the site and the points from which water and power can be taken. Everything required for the execution of the work which is not so specified is:

options.A: Provided by the Railways as and when the contractor demands it during execution
options.B: Within the scope of the contractor, to be arranged by him at his own cost as part of his contract obligation
options.C: Met from the provision for contingencies in the sanctioned estimate in all cases
options.D: Arranged by the Tender Committee after the work is awarded

q: The 'weathering course' provided over the roof slab of a building consists of:

options.A: A coat of waterproofing compound painted over the finished roof surface
options.B: A layer of tiles fixed over the slab for the appearance of the roof
options.C: A layer of concrete laid over the roof slab with a slope for draining off rain water, which protects the slab from the effects of the weather
options.D: The reinforcement cover provided over the top steel of the roof slab

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Funds allotted for a work which are not required for it are surrendered, so that they become available for allotment for other purposes.
2. Re-appropriation is the transfer of funds from one work or head to another within the same grant, made by the authority competent to do so, without the funds being surrendered.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: 'Sheet piles' used in foundation and excavation work are:

options.A: Short piles driven under a footing to compact the soil below it
options.B: Piles cast in place in bore holes made in the ground
options.C: Timber baulks laid horizontally to support the sides of a trench
options.D: Interlocking planks or sections of timber, steel or concrete driven vertically into the ground to form a continuous wall which retains the earth or excludes water

q: Under Section 73 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, the compensation recoverable for the breach of a contract is limited to the loss or damage which:

options.A: Naturally arose in the usual course of things from the breach, or which the parties knew, when they made the contract, to be likely to result from its breach
options.B: Is claimed by the injured party, whether or not it could have been foreseen when the contract was made
options.C: Arises from remote and indirect consequences of the breach in every case
options.D: Is fixed by the Engineer under the conditions of the contract

q: In the 'rise and fall' method of reducing the levels recorded in levelling work:

options.A: The reduced level of every point is worked out from the height of the instrument at each setting
options.B: The difference between each pair of successive staff readings is worked out as a rise or a fall, the reduced levels are derived successively from those differences, and the method provides a complete arithmetical check on the work
options.C: Only the first and the last points of the line are levelled, the intermediate points being interpolated
options.D: The levels are reduced by plotting them on a longitudinal section and reading off the values

q: During deep excavation for a work adjoining existing structures, the duty of the contractor in regard to those structures is that:

options.A: The structures are protected by the Railways at their own cost in every case
options.B: The contractor may undercut the adjoining structures, their support being restored after the work
options.C: Any damage to the adjoining structures is borne by their owners
options.D: The contractor must shore up, support and protect the adjoining structures and services during the excavation, and is liable for damage caused by his failure to do so
